text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a batch of legacy CSV exports landed in `crm_imports/legacy_exports/2026-03` and a bunch of field mappings are wrong. Playbook automation fired for ~12 accounts, so heads-up.

devon: @maya saw a couple. Looks like the importer slug normalization from the migration renamed `engagement_score` -> `engagement__score` (double underscore). Importer used to preserve original headers for legacy exports.

josiah: can you paste a sample row? want to see if it's a systematic rename or just a subset.

maya: sample snippet: ```
account_id,engagement_score,last_touch
12345,0.78,2026-03-17
```

devon: confirmed. The legacy pipeline regex in `legacy_adapter.py` changed to kebab/snake normalization. Quick fix: add a compatibility mapper that remaps the old header names before playbook triggers. I can open a PR.

samira: FYI this caused the renewal-alert playbook to auto-queue 3 accounts as high-risk. I've paused outbound sequences for that cohort and notified AMs. :handshake:

sync-bot: export_runner: Finished import job run-20260321-7 — 48 rows processed, 12 mapping warnings, 0 critical errors.

josh: can we run a targeted healthscore recalculation once mappings are fixed? I can trigger a backfill for affected account_ids.

devon: I'll push a tiny mapper + unit tests now and include a one-off migration script to rename the keys back. ETA ~2 hours. @josh please run the backfill after PR merge.

maya: added this to the CS incident tracker and linked runbook: https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/cs-import-mapping. Please drop short postmortem after resolution.

samira: filing a small request to devex to add a guard in playbook automation: don't trigger renewal-watch for records with `source=legacy_export` without manual review — ticket ENG-4821 created.

devon: thanks — will @channel when PR is merged and when migration completes. :thumbsup:
